plan.topic: Bloated or gassy after a big holiday meal on tirzepatide: what the US label reports (abdominal distension and flatulence vs placebo, if printed) and gentle habits that may help
plan.angle: Keep the angle as written, with these changes. (1) Title: 'Tirzepatide (Zepbound): Bloated After the Big Dinner? #shorts'. Don't use the Mounjaro brand, because the rates come from the Zepbound label. (2) Relief fact by 6 s, spoken as one rounded number per sentence after re-checking Zepbound PI Table 2 (rev 28 Aug 2026). For example: 'In the label's weight trials, about four in a hundred people on the top dose reported bloating. On placebo, it was about two in a hundred.' Put the full per-arm figures on screen only: abdominal distension 2% placebo vs 3% / 3% / 4%; flatulence 2% placebo vs 3% / 3% / 4% (5 / 10 / 15 mg). Use the label's population wording: 'adults with obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related condition'. (3) Remove the fallback line. If a GI-course sentence is used, it must be the label's exact wording: 'The majority of nausea, vomiting, and/or diarrhea events occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time.' Never apply it to bloating or constipation. (4) Keep 'tirzepatide delays gastric emptying' as its own sentence, not linked to bloating as the cause. (5) Low-blood-sugar line: 'If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea, ask your prescriber about holiday meals.' (6) The emergency line, the don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.', the loop line, 160 words or fewer, no subscribe or link line, and the Exp G post note to the Side Effects long video all stay as written.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): Bloated After the Big Dinner? #shorts
plan.why: Replaces the held S3 with a new felt holiday symptom that the label can verify and that we haven't covered in 30 days. It also feeds the Side Effects long video, which earns most of our watch time. | fact-check: This is a safe topic that fits the channel's focus and the evidence supports it. I checked the Zepbound US Prescribing Information on DailyMed (setid 487cd7e7-434c-4925-99fa-aa80b1cc776b, revised 28 Aug 2026). Section 6.1 Table 2 lists both terms. As read back by the fetch tool: abdominal distension is 2% placebo vs 3% / 3% / 4% (5 / 10 / 15 mg). Flatulence is 2% placebo vs 3% / 3% / 4%. The scriptwriter must open the table and confirm each per-arm figure before using it. Because the rates are printed, the primary path holds and the fallback isn't needed. But the fallback wording in the angle is wrong and must not be used: the label's sentence is 'The majority of nausea, vomiting, and/or diarrhea events occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time.' It does not cover constipation, and it never says 'mostly'. The pooled 6.1 population is the label's own wording ('adults with obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbid condition'). Copy it exactly and don't add 'without diabetes', because one of the pooled studies (Study 2) enrolled adults with type 2 diabetes. The working title says 'Mounjaro', but the data come from the Zepbound label, so the brand has to be Zepbound. The emergency line matches the tirzepatide Medication Guide wording ('with or without vomiting'). The low-blood-sugar caveat is fine. It may also say that low blood sugar has been reported in adults without type 2 diabetes. The difference from placebo is small (1–2 points), so call it 'reported slightly more than placebo', not 'common'. Don't present slower stomach emptying as the cause of bloating; keep it as a separate label sentence, as the angle already says. The tips must not drift into 'eat less' or restriction messaging.

package.title: Tirzepatide: Bloated After Holiday Dinner? #shorts
package.description:
Bloating was reported in tirzepatide's US label weight trials, but not often: about 4% on 15 mg vs 2% on placebo. Gas showed the same pattern, slightly more than placebo. Both trials were in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition (study 1 excluded type 2 diabetes; study 2 was type 2 diabetes only). If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea, ask your prescriber about holiday meals.

If severe stomach pain that won't go away happens, with or without vomiting, call your healthcare provider right away. For anything that isn't that emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.

#Tirzepatide

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary: This Short passes. Every number and label quote matches the Zepbound US label on DailyMed (revised 8/2026). Table 1 pools Study 1 and Study 2, with up to 72 weeks of treatment. Abdominal distension: placebo 2%, 5 mg 3%, 10 mg 3%, 15 mg 4%. Flatulence: the same, 2%, 3%, 3%, 4%. So "about four in a hundred on the top dose vs about two on placebo" and "gas, same pattern" are correct. Section 12.2 says word for word: "Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying. The delay is largest after the first dose and this effect diminishes over time." The script gives this as a separate label fact, not as the cause of bloating. The trial population is complete, including the weight-related condition and the split between Study 1 (no type 2 diabetes) and Study 2 (type 2 diabetes only). The pancreatitis line keeps the tirzepatide wording "with or without vomiting" and "right away", and uses the scoped don't-stop line for a single sign. The closing has no subscribe line and no link line. By my count the narration is 158 words, under the 160 limit; the task doesn't say which length arm applies, so I couldn't check that. The eating tips are hedged as "may help", are not restrictive, and add a caveat for people on insulin or a sulfonylurea. I found two minor wording issues and give exact fixes below.

issues.claim: Bloating: 4% on tirzepatide 15 mg vs 2% on placebo (label weight trials)
issues.problem: This fails the muted-viewer test: the stat card doesn't show the population or the timeframe. The population first appears in s03, and the label table covers up to 72 weeks.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Bloating (abdominal distension): 4% on tirzepatide 15 mg vs 2% on placebo, up to 72 weeks, adults with obesity or overweight with a weight-related condition (label Studies 1 and 2)"

issues.claim: One more label fact. Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying.
issues.problem: This comes straight after the bloating stats, so viewers may still read it as the cause. Adding the label's next sentence makes it a neutral fact and matches the on-screen item.
issues.fix: Replace with: "One more label fact. Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying. The label says that delay is largest after the first dose and lessens over time." (This adds 13 words, for about 171 in total, which is over the 160-word limit. Cut "Bloating was reported, but not often." in s02, or drop "The label says", to get back to 160 or fewer.)
